lines.say: Your bank card has no battery. So how does it talk to the card machine the moment you tap?
lines.show: Your bank card has *no battery.* So how does it [talk to the card machine] the moment you tap?

lines.say: The machine powers the card, by making an invisible magnetic field that keeps changing.
lines.show: The *machine* powers the card, by making an invisible *magnetic field* that [keeps changing.]

lines.say: Hidden around the edge of your card is a coil of wire. Bring it close, and that field creates just enough electricity in the coil to wake the chip.
lines.show: Hidden around the edge of your card is a *coil of wire.* Bring it close, and that field creates just enough electricity in the coil to [wake the chip.]

lines.say: The chip answers through the same field. It doesn't just send your card number. It adds a one-time code that only works for this payment.
lines.show: The chip answers through the same field. It doesn't just send your card number. It adds a *one-time code* that [only works for this payment.]

lines.say: Usually, the machine sends that to your bank, which checks the code and approves or declines, within seconds.
lines.show: Usually, the machine sends that to your *bank,* which checks the code and *approves* or declines, [within seconds.]

lines.say: In twenty fourteen, London let people tap bank cards straight onto the Tube. But a gate can't wait for the bank. So it checks that the card is genuine right there, fast enough for you to keep walking. The bank checks the payment later.
lines.show: In 2014, London let people tap *bank cards* straight onto the *Tube.* But a gate can't wait for the bank. So it checks that the card is *genuine* right there, [fast enough for you to keep walking.] The bank checks the payment later.

lines.say: So before the machine can take your money, it has to give your card something first: electricity.
lines.show: So before the machine can take your money, it has to give your card something first: [electricity.]

lines.say: Follow for how everyday tech really works.
lines.show: Follow for how [everyday tech] really works.
